pathway.title: Allison Transmission Holdings Inc — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: First (Documentary Fact). Total debt to trailing Adjusted EBITDA peaked at 3.59x at the first quarter of 2026 and was 2.82x at the third quarter, against 2.57x at year-end 2025; net debt to trailing Adjusted EBITDA was 2.47x against 1.25x. Leverage has stepped up and is coming down, so the trajectory rather than the level supports the credit.

Second (Documentary Fact). Liquidity of USD 1,493 million covers the USD 300 million of 2027 notes about five times (calculation B2), and the revolver is undrawn. Refinancing risk is low through 2027, though the 2029 to 2033 maturities are larger.

Third (Analyst Interpretation). With 30 September 2026 rates held constant, annual cash interest on funded debt is about USD 203 million (calculation B1), and trailing Adjusted EBITDA covers it 7.04x, against 7.73x on trailing cash interest paid. The financial base said a run-rate could not be calculated without a rate path; holding quarter-end rates constant it can be estimated, and it is lower than the trailing figure.

Fourth (Analyst Interpretation). Earnings would have to fall about 85% before the first lien covenant ratio reached 5.50x (calculation B3). The covenant gives lenders little early warning and does not constrain distributions.

Fifth (Documentary Fact). Adjusted free cash flow of USD 662 million exceeded dividends and repurchases of USD 195 million by USD 467 million for nine months (calculation B4), which is about 13% of net debt. Retained cash is the main source of further debt reduction.

Sixth (Documentary Fact). Each quarterly report gives unaudited pro forma net sales and net income as if the acquisition had occurred on 2025-01-01, which corrects the earlier statements that none existed. Derived sales of the acquired unit grew 4.1% in the third quarter and 7.6% for nine months over the same periods of 2025, so the unit is not shrinking on a derived basis; its earnings before interest and depreciation are still unknown.

Seventh (Analyst Interpretation). The reported covenant ratio matches term loans less all cash over reported trailing Adjusted EBITDA, with no pro forma credit for the acquired unit's earlier quarters. The covenant measures reported earnings, so it does not capture a full year of the acquired unit's earnings.

runs.text: Strength, franchise margin (Documentary Fact). The legacy Allison Transmission unit earned an Adjusted EBITDA margin of 37.8% in the third quarter of 2026, well above the 12.7% of the acquired unit, so it carries most of group earnings.

Strength, revenue visibility (Documentary Fact). Long-term agreements with OEMs cover over 90% of North American on-highway unit volume and run three to five years; they set pricing and commodity cost sharing but not committed volume.
Strength, liquidity (Documentary Fact). Cash of USD 497 million and revolver availability of USD 996 million give USD 1,493 million, with nothing drawn on the revolver, which matures in January 2031.

Strength, covenant headroom (Documentary Fact). The single maintenance test, a maximum first lien net leverage ratio of 5.50x, was 0.84x at 30 September 2026; it is tested when revolving loan commitments remain outstanding and is reproduced from filed numbers.
Strength, cash generation and deleveraging (Documentary Fact). Adjusted free cash flow was USD 662 million for nine months 2026; the revolver was repaid and USD 100 million of notes redeemed.

Strength, debt structure (Documentary Fact). Maturities are spread: USD 300 million in 2027, USD 500 million in 2029, USD 1,505 million in 2031 and USD 1,694 million in 2033, with USD 2,300 million of fixed-rate notes.

Strength, end-market balance (Analyst Interpretation). Defense and aftermarket sales add counter-cyclical stability, and the acquisition added construction, agriculture, mining and industrial markets, though management describes industrial and agriculture demand as subdued.
Weakness, acquisition leverage (Documentary Fact). Net debt rose from USD 1,414 million at year-end 2025 to USD 3,540 million at 30 September 2026 on the note-total debt measure.

Weakness, perimeter mismatch (Insufficient Information). Trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,431 million holds the acquired unit for only three quarters; pro forma net sales and net income exist but pro forma Adjusted EBITDA does not, so combined leverage is Not calculable.

Weakness, lower-margin and cyclical acquired unit (Documentary Fact). The acquired unit is 42.6% of third quarter net sales with a 12.7% margin, its purchase accounting is preliminary, and integration costs continue.

Weakness, customer concentration (Documentary Fact). The top five OEM customers were 52% of FY2025 net sales before the acquisition, with Daimler AG at 18%; the post-acquisition split is not supplied.
Weakness, shareholder returns (Management Language). Dividends and repurchases of USD 195 million for nine months 2026 continue while management states a 2.0x net leverage target without defining it.

Weakness, earnings definition (Documentary Fact). Adjusted EBITDA includes USD 200 million of adjustments for nine months, 17.2% of the reported figure, defined by a credit agreement that is not supplied.

Weakness, structure and documentation (Insufficient Information). Secured term loans of USD 1,699 million rank ahead of USD 2,300 million of unsecured notes; the guarantor roster is unresolved and legal documents are not supplied.

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: Transaction. On June 11, 2025 Allison entered into a stock purchase agreement with Dana Incorporated to acquire its off-highway business (S1 page:56). The acquisition closed on January 1, 2026. The final purchase price is 2,628 (S4 page:7), after a 34 reduction for net deficiency in cash, indebtedness and working capital against a preliminary closing payment (S4 page:7); the annual report gave approximately 2,732 as a preliminary figure (S1 page:118). The sources disagree on the price at different dates and the disagreement is logged below, not reconciled. The acquired business forms the whole Allison Off-Highway segment (S4 page:7). Preliminary purchase accounting allocates goodwill of 770, of which 132 to Allison Transmission and 638 to Allison Off-Highway, and identifiable intangibles of 875 (S4 page:7 and page:8); the fair values are subject to change up to one year from closing (S4 page:8). The company expects the acquisition to be accretive to net income and diluted earnings per share in 2026, a management expectation (S7 page:4).

Financing and use of proceeds. The price was paid with cash on hand, 500 of proceeds from 5.875% senior notes due December 2033 issued by ATI, 1,200 of an incremental term loan under the credit agreement, and 300 of borrowings on ATI's revolving credit facility (S4 page:6). Lenders had also committed to a 364-day senior unsecured bridge facility of up to 2,000; it was reduced to 500 by December 31, 2025, was never drawn and was terminated at closing (S4 page:6). The notes were issued in November 2025 as a private placement and the proceeds were designated for the acquisition (S1 page:104). Debt raised for the acquisition is therefore 2,000 on the printed components (calculation A1), against a net cash outlay for the acquisition of 2,563 in the first quarter, reduced to 2,529 for the nine months after the price adjustment (S5 page:8, S4 page:3). Cash on hand covered the balance, and cash fell from 1,495 at 2025-12-31 to 311 at 2026-03-31 (financial base handoff).

New debt issues and amendments. (1) 5.875% senior notes due December 2033, 500, issued November 2025 by ATI, unsecured; redeemable before December 1, 2028 at par plus an applicable premium (S4 page:23). (2) Amendment No. 5 to the credit agreement, entered January 2026 (dated January 2, 2026 in the annual report), added an incremental term loan of 1,200 maturing January 2, 2033 with a springing maturity to the term loan date if that is earlier, raised revolver commitments from 750 to 1,000 and extended the revolver maturity from March 2029 to January 2031 (S4 page:20, S1 page:119). The incremental term loan pays Term SOFR plus 1.75%, an all-in 5.54% at 2026-09-30 (S4 page:20). (3) Amendment No. 6, June 2026, lowered the margin on the original term loan by 0.25% (S4 page:20). (4) 300 was drawn on the revolver at closing, 150 was repaid in the first quarter and the remaining 150 in the second quarter (S5 page:1, S6 page:1). Deferred financing fees recorded on the amendment were 3 on the revolver increase and 12 on the incremental term loan (S4 page:20). Secured debt after the transaction is the two term loans, 1,699, against 2,300 of unsecured notes; the revolver is undrawn (financial base handoff). Liquidity effect: liquidity at 2026-09-30 is 1,493 on the financial base handoff, compared with 2,240 at 2025-12-31.

Status and gaps. The transaction is completed; integration and purchase accounting are open. The sale agreement, the credit agreement and its amendments, the note indentures and the commitment letter are not in the pack (context records legal documents as none), so conditions, indemnities, purchase price adjustment mechanics and any earn-out or deferred consideration are Not supplied. The 2.0x net leverage target stated by management is not defined in the pack, and the financial base handoff computes net leverage of 2.47x on a trailing reported basis that mixes perimeters, so the two are not comparable and no gap to target is stated here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On the filed numbers the credit is a lightly levered industrial that took on acquisition debt in the first quarter of 2026 and has been paying it down. Total debt at 2026-09-30 was 4,037 against 2,909 at 2025-12-31; cash fell from 1,495 to 497; net debt on the same debt measure therefore rose from 1,414 to 3,540. On trailing reported Adjusted EBITDA of 1,431 that is 2.82x gross and 2.47x net, down from a first-quarter peak of 3.59x and 3.33x and above the 2.57x and 1.25x at FY2025. Cash interest paid is covered 7.73x on a trailing basis. Liquidity at the quarter end is 1,493 (cash 497 plus 996 available under the 1,000 revolving facility, net of 4 of letters of credit), with no loans drawn on the revolver. The only financial maintenance covenant described is a maximum first lien net leverage ratio of 5.50x, reported at 0.84x, and the arithmetic of the filings reproduces that figure from term loans, cash and trailing Adjusted EBITDA. The weaknesses are perimeter and definition: trailing earnings contain the acquired business for only the 2026 quarters, so the leverage ratios overstate leverage against a full combined year and the interest cover may be flattered because only part of a year of the new interest cost is in the trailing cash figure; Adjusted EBITDA is a company and credit-agreement measure with material add-backs; the legal documents are not supplied; and purchase accounting is preliminary. Confidence is Medium overall and High for the reported balances.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit is a leading but cyclical industrial supplier that has become materially larger and more diversified through a debt-funded acquisition. The legacy Allison Transmission unit makes fully automatic transmissions for medium- and heavy-duty commercial vehicles and for medium and heavy tactical defense vehicles, sells mainly through long-term agreements with a concentrated group of OEMs, and earns margins far above the acquired Allison Off-Highway unit. The January 2026 acquisition of Dana Incorporated's off-highway business was paid for with new notes at ATI, a new secured term loan, a revolver draw and cash on hand, and added two reportable segments, a much larger global manufacturing footprint and a lower-margin, more cyclical earnings stream. For creditors, the mechanics that matter are: a high-margin core with long-term customer agreements and an aftermarket cushion; a customer base where the top five OEMs were over half of sales before the acquisition; a lower-margin acquired unit with preliminary purchase accounting and open integration costs; and secured acquisition debt that sits ahead of fixed-rate unsecured notes. The issuer is publicly held with no sponsor in the pack, and its documented behaviour since closing is to repay debt (revolver repaid, partial note redemption) while continuing dividends and buybacks, which is mixed rather than extraction-oriented. Legal capacity to change that behaviour cannot be judged because the debt documents are not supplied. This handoff also corrects the earlier handoffs on pro forma information, set out in the correction section below.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Transaction. On June 11, 2025 Allison entered into a stock purchase agreement with Dana Incorporated to acquire its off-highway business (S1 page:56). The acquisition closed on January 1, 2026. The final purchase price is 2,628 (S4 page:7), after a 34 reduction for net deficiency in cash, indebtedness and working capital against a preliminary closing payment (S4 page:7); the annual report gave approximately 2,732 as a preliminary figure (S1 page:118). The sources disagree on the price at different dates and the disagreement is logged below, not reconciled. The acquired business forms the whole Allison Off-Highway segment (S4 page:7). Preliminary purchase accounting allocates goodwill of 770, of which 132 to Allison Transmission and 638 to Allison Off-Highway, and identifiable intangibles of 875 (S4 page:7 and page:8); the fair values are subject to change up to one year from closing (S4 page:8). The company expects the acquisition to be accretive to net income and diluted earnings per share in 2026, a management expectation (S7 page:4).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financing and use of proceeds. The price was paid with cash on hand, 500 of proceeds from 5.875% senior notes due December 2033 issued by ATI, 1,200 of an incremental term loan under the credit agreement, and 300 of borrowings on ATI's revolving credit facility (S4 page:6). Lenders had also committed to a 364-day senior unsecured bridge facility of up to 2,000; it was reduced to 500 by December 31, 2025, was never drawn and was terminated at closing (S4 page:6). The notes were issued in November 2025 as a private placement and the proceeds were designated for the acquisition (S1 page:104). Debt raised for the acquisition is therefore 2,000 on the printed components (calculation A1), against a net cash outlay for the acquisition of 2,563 in the first quarter, reduced to 2,529 for the nine months after the price adjustment (S5 page:8, S4 page:3). Cash on hand covered the balance, and cash fell from 1,495 at 2025-12-31 to 311 at 2026-03-31 (financial base handoff).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New debt issues and amendments. (1) 5.875% senior notes due December 2033, 500, issued November 2025 by ATI, unsecured; redeemable before December 1, 2028 at par plus an applicable premium (S4 page:23). (2) Amendment No. 5 to the credit agreement, entered January 2026 (dated January 2, 2026 in the annual report), added an incremental term loan of 1,200 maturing January 2, 2033 with a springing maturity to the term loan date if that is earlier, raised revolver commitments from 750 to 1,000 and extended the revolver maturity from March 2029 to January 2031 (S4 page:20, S1 page:119). The incremental term loan pays Term SOFR plus 1.75%, an all-in 5.54% at 2026-09-30 (S4 page:20). (3) Amendment No. 6, June 2026, lowered the margin on the original term loan by 0.25% (S4 page:20). (4) 300 was drawn on the revolver at closing, 150 was repaid in the first quarter and the remaining 150 in the second quarter (S5 page:1, S6 page:1). Deferred financing fees recorded on the amendment were 3 on the revolver increase and 12 on the incremental term loan (S4 page:20). Secured debt after the transaction is the two term loans, 1,699, against 2,300 of unsecured notes; the revolver is undrawn (financial base handoff). Liquidity effect: liquidity at 2026-09-30 is 1,493 on the financial base handoff, compared with 2,240 at 2025-12-31.

fields.value: This is the fundamental credit synthesis for Allison Transmission Holdings Inc as of 2026-11-05, on the credit_snapshot pathway. Scope is business risk, financial risk, liquidity and the gaps that limit them, built only from the upstream handoffs, with no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The synthesis uses the three upstream handoffs below. They rest on the seven issuer sources listed, which were not re-read for new facts here; every figure is taken from the handoffs and carries their period and perimeter labels.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Run settings, not issuer evidence: context file 1411207-allison-transmission-holdings-inc-alsn.json, sha256 f65312705cd8bb204fde9755509326ba975099b166b8d246c949fcd0ea955b5a.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Allison Transmission Holdings is a solid mid-leverage industrial credit that is still working off acquisition debt. Its strongest support is a high-margin transmission franchise with long-term customer agreements, liquidity of USD 1,493 million with the revolver undrawn, and a first lien leverage ratio of 0.84x against a 5.50x limit. Its weakest point is leverage: total debt of USD 4,037 million is 2.82x trailing Adjusted EBITDA, a figure that mixes periods with and without the lower-margin off-highway business and cannot be restated on a combined basis. The outcome will be decided by how quickly operating cash flow retires debt while dividends and buybacks continue, by how the acquired business performs through a downturn, and by what the unseen credit agreement permits.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Allison combines a franchise with high margins and a long-term customer base with a large liquidity cushion, so acquisition leverage of 2.82x trailing is serviceable and falling, provided that the lower-margin acquired business holds its earnings and shareholder returns do not slow deleveraging.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength, franchise margin (Documentary Fact). The legacy Allison Transmission unit earned an Adjusted EBITDA margin of 37.8% in the third quarter of 2026, well above the 12.7% of the acquired unit, so it carries most of group earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength, revenue visibility (Documentary Fact). Long-term agreements with OEMs cover over 90% of North American on-highway unit volume and run three to five years; they set pricing and commodity cost sharing but not committed volume.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength, liquidity (Documentary Fact). Cash of USD 497 million and revolver availability of USD 996 million give USD 1,493 million, with nothing drawn on the revolver, which matures in January 2031.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength, covenant headroom (Documentary Fact). The single maintenance test, a maximum first lien net leverage ratio of 5.50x, was 0.84x at 30 September 2026; it is tested when revolving loan commitments remain outstanding and is reproduced from filed numbers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength, cash generation and deleveraging (Documentary Fact). Adjusted free cash flow was USD 662 million for nine months 2026; the revolver was repaid and USD 100 million of notes redeemed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength, debt structure (Documentary Fact). Maturities are spread: USD 300 million in 2027, USD 500 million in 2029, USD 1,505 million in 2031 and USD 1,694 million in 2033, with USD 2,300 million of fixed-rate notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength, end-market balance (Analyst Interpretation). Defense and aftermarket sales add counter-cyclical stability, and the acquisition added construction, agriculture, mining and industrial markets, though management describes industrial and agriculture demand as subdued.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness, acquisition leverage (Documentary Fact). Net debt rose from USD 1,414 million at year-end 2025 to USD 3,540 million at 30 September 2026 on the note-total debt measure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness, perimeter mismatch (Insufficient Information). Trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,431 million holds the acquired unit for only three quarters; pro forma net sales and net income exist but pro forma Adjusted EBITDA does not, so combined leverage is Not calculable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness, lower-margin and cyclical acquired unit (Documentary Fact). The acquired unit is 42.6% of third quarter net sales with a 12.7% margin, its purchase accounting is preliminary, and integration costs continue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness, customer concentration (Documentary Fact). The top five OEM customers were 52% of FY2025 net sales before the acquisition, with Daimler AG at 18%; the post-acquisition split is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness, shareholder returns (Management Language). Dividends and repurchases of USD 195 million for nine months 2026 continue while management states a 2.0x net leverage target without defining it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness, earnings definition (Documentary Fact). Adjusted EBITDA includes USD 200 million of adjustments for nine months, 17.2% of the reported figure, defined by a credit agreement that is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness, structure and documentation (Insufficient Information). Secured term loans of USD 1,699 million rank ahead of USD 2,300 million of unsecured notes; the guarantor roster is unresolved and legal documents are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: First (Documentary Fact). Total debt to trailing Adjusted EBITDA peaked at 3.59x at the first quarter of 2026 and was 2.82x at the third quarter, against 2.57x at year-end 2025; net debt to trailing Adjusted EBITDA was 2.47x against 1.25x. Leverage has stepped up and is coming down, so the trajectory rather than the level supports the credit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Second (Documentary Fact). Liquidity of USD 1,493 million covers the USD 300 million of 2027 notes about five times (calculation B2), and the revolver is undrawn. Refinancing risk is low through 2027, though the 2029 to 2033 maturities are larger.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Third (Analyst Interpretation). With 30 September 2026 rates held constant, annual cash interest on funded debt is about USD 203 million (calculation B1), and trailing Adjusted EBITDA covers it 7.04x, against 7.73x on trailing cash interest paid. The financial base said a run-rate could not be calculated without a rate path; holding quarter-end rates constant it can be estimated, and it is lower than the trailing figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fourth (Analyst Interpretation). Earnings would have to fall about 85% before the first lien covenant ratio reached 5.50x (calculation B3). The covenant gives lenders little early warning and does not constrain distributions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fifth (Documentary Fact). Adjusted free cash flow of USD 662 million exceeded dividends and repurchases of USD 195 million by USD 467 million for nine months (calculation B4), which is about 13% of net debt. Retained cash is the main source of further debt reduction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sixth (Documentary Fact). Each quarterly report gives unaudited pro forma net sales and net income as if the acquisition had occurred on 2025-01-01, which corrects the earlier statements that none existed. Derived sales of the acquired unit grew 4.1% in the third quarter and 7.6% for nine months over the same periods of 2025, so the unit is not shrinking on a derived basis; its earnings before interest and depreciation are still unknown.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Seventh (Analyst Interpretation). The reported covenant ratio matches term loans less all cash over reported trailing Adjusted EBITDA, with no pro forma credit for the acquired unit's earlier quarters. The covenant measures reported earnings, so it does not capture a full year of the acquired unit's earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Source readiness stated that a search of all sources found no pro forma disclosure, and the financial base stated that results of the acquired business for 2025 were not supplied and that a run-rate interest cover was not calculable. The business and transaction handoff corrected the first point: each quarterly report has supplemental pro forma net sales and net income. This handoff refines the second: holding 30 September 2026 rates constant, run-rate cash interest can be estimated (calculation B1), although it remains an estimate that excludes fees, hedges and interest income. Pro forma Adjusted EBITDA, pro forma interest and any fourth quarter 2025 pro forma figure remain Not supplied, so the conclusion that combined leverage is Not calculable stands.

fields.value: The credit work for Allison Transmission Holdings Inc is well sourced and committee use is restricted, not blocked. Of the 21 claims traced in the credit driver table below, 19 are verified to a filed page and recompute exactly, 1 is verified with a rounding correction (third quarter interest cover) and 1 is an estimate that rests on stated assumptions (run-rate cash interest). Every derived figure in the financial base, business and transaction and synthesis handoffs was recomputed; the only arithmetic discrepancy is the 7.73x that should be 7.74x. One factual statement in the source readiness and financial base handoffs, that no pro forma disclosure existed, is wrong: each quarterly report has a pro forma note (S2 page:9, S3 page:9, S4 page:9). The business and transaction and synthesis handoffs corrected it, and this review confirms the correction. The earlier handoffs cannot be edited, so readers should use the corrected statement. The restrictions that remain are structural: no executed legal documents, no pro forma earnings before interest and depreciation, an unresolved guarantor roster and preliminary purchase accounting. No source is dated after the 2026-11-05 cutoff, and subsequent events are labelled as such.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against the synthesis view of a moderate and improving credit is the perimeter mismatch: trailing Adjusted EBITDA holds the acquired unit for three of four quarters, so reported leverage is overstated, yet the acquired unit earns a 12.7% Adjusted EBITDA margin against 37.8% for the legacy unit, so a full year would add less earnings than its sales share suggests (S7 page:10). A second counterpoint is that management's 2.0x net leverage target is below the 2.47x computed on the reported trailing basis, while distributions of 195 over nine months continue. Both would win if the pro forma earnings were weak or if the credit agreement allowed large distributions, which the pack cannot show.
